description: We are some Makers from outer space! Kerala's our earthly hangout, nestled in India. Since India's chillin' on Earth, and Earth is floating in space, guess what? We're basically space adventurers!
summary:
It is an Interactive Mars Survival and Mission Training Simulator. DUSTFALL combines story-driven gameplay with NASA's Martian environmental science to help young explorers understand the challenges of operating a planetary outpost.
Through MARS-EIS, real scientific observations can inform environmental conditions, while interactive survival mechanics teach resource management, engineering trade-offs, and scientific decision-making.
details:
Our project, DUSTFALL, powered by the Mars Environmental Intelligence and Simulation Engine (MARS-EIS), is an interactive Mars survival simulation developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Kochi. It combines scientific environmental modelling, artificial intelligence, and gameplay to demonstrate the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars.

MARS-EIS simulates Martian atmospheric conditions, dust storms, solar radiation, temperature variations, and habitat infrastructure using physics-based models and real observational data from NASA missions. AI models (GRU and Isolation Forest) provide environmental forecasting and anomaly detection. DUSTFALL presents these simulations through a 2D survival game where players respond to emergencies, repair infrastructure, manage resources, and protect the crew.

The project uses Python, Pygame, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch, FastAPI, WebSockets, NetworkX, SQLite, and with optional CUDA GPU acceleration.

Its key innovation is modelling cascading environmental consequences rather than relying on scripted events. For example, dust storms reduce solar power generation, causing battery depletion and threatening habitat operations.

Our intended impact is to promote planetary science education and provide a foundation for exploring Mars habitat resilience, environmental risks, and sustainable human exploration. We prioritised scientific accuracy, computational efficiency, modularity, scalability, and accessibility.
